intro: Childcare builds patience, care and coordination that early education and health support jobs value. The closest of the 25 careers below is Preschool Teachers, Except Special Education, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $38,140, which is 9% more than childcare workers earn.
why_it_works: Caring for young children means noticing small changes in mood, keeping routines and working with parents. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.38 out of 5 for this job, close to what aides in health and therapy settings need. About half of the matches need no new schooling. Others, such as kindergarten teaching, need a degree but pay much more than the $34,980 childcare median.
tips: Get or renew your CPR and first aid certificates; aide jobs in schools and clinics often ask for them.
Look at occupational therapy assistant programs: the job earns $72,300, which is 107% more than childcare pay.
Document lesson plans and developmental notes you write; they show readiness for preschool teaching.

faq.q: What jobs can former childcare workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are preschool teachers (88%), Psychiatric Aides (74%) and School Bus Monitors (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Kindergarten teachers are also a 73% match and earn $62,680, which is 79% more than the $34,980 childcare median, though they usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Which careers for childcare workers pay more?
faq.a: 18 of the 25 matches pay more than childcare work. The largest gains are secondary special education teachers at $74,260 (112% more), Occupational Therapy Assistants at $72,300 (107% more) and preschool special education teachers at $64,830 (85% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do childcare workers need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: About 15 of the 25 matches need no more education than childcare workers already have, including aide roles. The best-paid teaching options usually need a degree. In the closest match, 29% of workers have a high school diploma as their highest level.

faq.q: What skills should childcare workers develop?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, managing money, instructing and managing materials. Your social perceptiveness already rates 3.25 out of 5 in O*NET, so building teaching and planning skills is the main step toward better-paid roles.
